summary: Justin sits bottom of the table on 80 points, so his GW4 claims process first when the window closes on 11 September. Today's full round of matches turned up three genuine surprises the model doesn't see yet - Bijol and Igor Jesus both left out of their sides' matchday squads for the first time this season, and Brentford's Collins forced off with a calf strain of unknown severity - reshaping the board to three defensive moves (Munoz, Bijol, a low-confidence Collins hedge) alongside the standing midfield claims for the still-unintegrated Barcola and the still-injured Doku. Igor Jesus itself drops out as a target rather than in, since he wasn't even in Forest's 18 today.

claims.why: Barcola remains unintegrated at Liverpool: manager Andoni Iraola said before naming him among the substitutes for Friday's trip to Ipswich (his actual first appearance for the club) that 'he hasn't had the minutes in the preseason games'. Le Fee, by contrast, started today's 1-1 draw at Brentford, hit the post from range in the first half and scored the equalising penalty in the 82nd minute - a first-choice starter in form.
claims.model: Model has Le Fee at next5 16.5 (avail 1.00) versus Barcola at 2.3 (avail 0.16) - most of that gap is the model having zero career data on a mid-season GBP123m arrival, exactly the blind spot today's news fills in. Agree with overruling the model's placeholder rating for Barcola.

sources.title: Andoni Iraola: Bradley Barcola could make Liverpool debut against Ipswich
Brentford 1-1 Sunderland: Enzo Le Fee penalty cancels out Vitaly Janelt opener but Bees' unbeaten start continues

claims.why: Doku was not even named in Manchester City's 18 for today's 1-0 win over Coventry, still out with the calf injury picked up in the Community Shield defeat to Arsenal, with Rayan Cherki continuing in his place in the number 10 role. Return estimates point to City's 13 September fixture at the earliest - after GW4's own deadline - so he offers nothing for this window.
claims.model: Model has Rayan at next5 15.8 (avail 0.95) versus Doku at 4.5 (avail 0.16) - the model already prices the injury in heavily; agree with the swap, reinforced by today's confirmed absence.

sources.title: Starting Lineups - Man City vs Coventry

claims.why: Munoz was again an impact substitute rather than a starter today - on for Ola Aina in the 59th minute of Forest's goalless draw with Tottenham - not the nailed-on right wing-back his permanent transfer suggested. Hill remains a guaranteed starter in Bournemouth's back line with no such competition.
claims.model: Model has Hill at next5 16.0 (avail 0.97) versus Munoz at 7.0 (avail 0.37) - a wide gap the model already prices in via low availability; agree, and today's bench role reinforces it further.

sources.title: Starting Lineups - N Forest vs Spurs

claims.why: Bijol was left out of Leeds' starting XI at Brighton today for the first time this season - Nico Elvedi and Tarik Muharemovic started in central defence instead, with Bijol introduced only in the 61st minute. It is one match, but with a new arrival now preferred ahead of him his starting spot no longer looks nailed on.
claims.model: Model has Botman at next5 15.6 (avail 1.00) versus Bijol at 15.4 (avail 0.92) - a small numbers gap on its own, but today's team news is the real reason for this claim rather than the model's number. Medium rather than high confidence since it is only one match so far.

claims.why: Speculative hedge: Brentford captain Nathan Collins was forced off with a calf strain after just 17 minutes of today's draw with Sunderland, and manager Keith Andrews said 'it's a calf strain, I don't know the extent'. If it turns out to be more than a knock, this claim covers a fit, confirmed-starting alternative; if it is minor, this is the one to skip.
claims.model: Model has Richards at next5 15.6 (avail 1.00) versus Collins at 16.5 (avail 1.00) - the model still rates Collins the stronger player and does not yet reflect today's injury at all, so this claim rests entirely on the news, not the numbers. Low confidence, submit last.

sources.title: Nathan Collins injury update after Brentford v Sunderland

claims.why: Woltemade left Newcastle for Juventus on a season-long loan on deadline day, so he plays in Serie A, not the Premier League, until at least next summer - a mandatory drop, not a judgement call. Igor Jesus is confirmed as Forest's starting striker in their predicted XI for Friday's game against Tottenham.
claims.model: Model: Igor Jesus next5 14.5 vs Woltemade 0.3, +14.2. Fully agree - the loan has pushed Woltemade's number to essentially zero, the clearest drop in the squad.

claims.why: Eze is still stuck behind Arsenal's front line under Arteta with no sign of a minutes trend pointing up. Rayan is confirmed in Bournemouth's predicted attacking three alongside Kluivert and Tavernier for the Newcastle game, and is being talked up as a breakout name this season.
claims.model: Model: Rayan next5 16.2 vs Eze 8.0, +8.2. Agree with the model - Eze's bench role explains the gap and there is no sign of it closing.

sources.title: Could Bournemouth's Rayan become the Premier League's next Brazilian star?

claims.why: This is a hedge, not an urgent need. Garner's recovery from groin surgery is running ahead of schedule and he started for Everton in midweek against Preston, but Moyes still is not trusting him for a full 90 minutes. Gross is a fully fit, nailed-on Brighton starter with no fitness question at all. Only use this claim if you want the safer floor rather than Garner's upside.
claims.model: Model: Gross next5 16.0 vs Garner 10.1, +5.9. Partial overrule - the model cannot see Garner's accelerated recovery, so the real gap is probably smaller than 5.9, but Gross is nailed and Garner still is not.

runs.note: first run - four claims submitted (Munoz drop upgraded from yesterday's hold after fresh reporting on his Aina competition); a fifth was not included since the rest of the squad is either performing above its model rating (Marmoush, kept) or has no clear replacement worth the waiver priority this week

No material change since the last run 18 minutes ago. Refreshed sourcing - confirmed Igor Jesus as Forest's starting striker ahead of Chris Wood, and Bournemouth's Hill, Rayan and Tavernier all in the latest predicted XI - and confirmed Bijol is not a drop risk since his two rivals for the Leeds centre-back shirt (Rodon, Gruev) are both injured. Still no fifth claim: Marmoush's real starting role beats his model rating and the rest of the squad is performing at or above its number.

No change to the four claims after a full club-by-club refresh - the model's numbers for every add/drop pair are unchanged and every squad member's situation (Munoz vs Aina, Woltemade in Serie A, Eze benched, Garner's careful reintroduction, Bijol's injured rivals) still checks out. The one new find was a pundit piece projecting Marmoush inside Tottenham's actual strongest XI going forward, reinforcing rather than changing the decision to keep him over a fifth claim.

Dropped the Hill-for-Munoz claim: Forest's own predicted XI (published this morning) has Munoz starting at right wing-back against Spurs, not competing with Aina, so he is no longer a drop candidate and no other squad DEF clears the swap bar. Igor Jesus/Woltemade, Rayan/Eze and Gross/Garner carried forward unchanged after a full club-by-club refresh; also checked Barcola (now live in the pool, possible bench debut Friday at Ipswich) but no squad MID is weak enough to justify dropping for him.

First run for the GW4 window (GW3 waivers have processed and the squad moved on since last week's file, which is now filed under previous). Four claims: Igor Jesus for Marmoush (Forest's confirmed #1 striker over Wood vs a Marmoush facing real competition from Solanke), Ampadu for Garner (Garner was a sub, not a starter, at Preston as earlier reported, and is behind Hackney for Sunday), Le Fee for Barcola (Barcola confirmed bench for his Liverpool debut), and a low-confidence Rayan for Doku (Doku's return is pegged for right around this gameweek, so it's a hedge). No fifth claim - the rest of the defense and attack are confirmed starters outperforming their model numbers.

No change. Re-checked all four adds and drops (Igor Jesus/Marmoush, Ampadu/Garner, Le Fee/Barcola, Rayan/Doku) plus rivals across a fresh club-by-club sweep 13 minutes after the last update - Forest's Munoz/Milenkovic, Rodon's hamstring, Doku's calf timeline and Barcola's expected bench debut at Ipswich all check out exactly as before. Still no fifth claim; the rest of the squad remains confirmed starters above their model numbers.

Dropped Ampadu for Garner: Garner is now confirmed set to start against Man Utd (Hackney a doubt with a knock), reversing last night's bench read, and no other squad midfielder or defender is weak enough once confirmed starting roles are accounted for. Kept Igor Jesus/Marmoush (reworded - Solanke's ankle injury has actually improved Marmoush's own case, so this is now a value upgrade not a bench-risk swap) and Le Fee/Barcola and Rayan/Doku unchanged. Three claims this week, down from four.

Re-sourced all three claims after today's SOURCES-list purge stripped their citations - real permitted links are back for Igor Jesus/Marmoush, Le Fee/Barcola and Rayan/Doku. Also upgraded Rayan/Doku from low to medium confidence: Doku's calf return now points to around 13 September, which is after GW4's own deadline (12 September), so this is no longer just a timing hedge. No change to which three claims are made.

No change. Fresh club-by-club sweep ~8 hours later re-confirmed all three claims (Igor Jesus/Marmoush, Le Fee/Barcola, Rayan/Doku) plus checked Bijol, Garner and the rest of the squad for anything that would open a fourth claim - nothing did. Reports naming Aina ahead of Munoz at Forest right wing-back surfaced but only through unpermitted outlets, so Munoz was not added as a drop candidate on that alone.

Reordered rather than changed: Le Fee/Barcola and Rayan/Doku swap to ranks 1-2 (Barcola still bench-bound for today's Ipswich debut, Doku still out for today's Coventry game) and Igor Jesus/Marmoush drops to rank 3 at low confidence, since Marmoush is now a confirmed Tottenham starter alongside Igor Jesus at Forest, leaving this as a pure model-number swap rather than a bench-risk case. Also confirmed via Palace's own site that Mateta is out three weeks with a hamstring injury, which secures Strand Larsen's role further but does not open a fourth claim since he is already kept, not dropped. No other squad member's situation changed.

Full round of GW3 matches produced real news the model can't see: Igor Jesus was not even in Forest's 18 today (Delap started, Wood the sub), killing the Igor Jesus/Marmoush claim outright since Marmoush started and played 84 minutes for Spurs - dropped rather than replaced, since Marmoush is now clearly the stronger, more secure player of the two. In its place, two fresh DEF claims from today's confirmed lineups: Bijol was benched for the first time this season at Leeds (Elvedi/Muharemovic started), and Munoz was again only an impact sub at Forest, reinforcing his existing low model rating - both sourced directly off Sky Sports lineup pages rather than predicted-XI aggregators. A fifth, low-confidence claim was added on the back of Nathan Collins' calf strain (forced off after 17 minutes for Brentford, severity unknown) as a hedge, since the model does not yet reflect it at all. Le Fee/Barcola and Rayan/Doku carried forward with fresh sourcing (Le Fee's penalty and man-of-the-match display, Doku confirmed absent from City's 18 vs Coventry) and Le Fee/Barcola upgraded to high confidence given how comprehensively Barcola remains unintegrated.
